## p162 A1 — Repeated Munich courier departure notice

**Edition context:** Munich couriers carrying radio operating documents.

**Related source pages:** [p151 D2](151.md#source-p151-d2), [p153 D2](153.md#source-p153-d2), [p153 E1](153.md#source-p153-e1), [p158 C2](158.md#source-p158-c2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-munich-couriers-carrying-radio-operating-documents"></a>


[Source and certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/README.md)

Five records intercepted on 9 November concern couriers carrying radio operating documents to Munich: first parts p153 E1 / p162 A1 and continuations p151 D2 / p153 D2 / p158 C2. The best continuation fixes **67 of 68 positions** under the published Nov7–9 key; the damaged first part has a conditional 134-position reconstruction. The unit numeral remains **{5,6}** in the key, with a historical argument for **6** below.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

The first part is an editorial reconstruction with the source costs below:

**Readable German:**

> An Ingenieurinspektion Muenchen. Gefr. Geraus und Feldgr. Mahrer als
> Kurier mit Funkbetriebsunterlagen fuer Grukonach{5,6}02 7 Uhr abds.
> nach dort abgefahren.

The best-preserved second-part witness, p158 C2, reads directly without any
source-coordinate change:

**Readable German:**

> Grukonach{5,6}02 benachrichtigen. Eintreffen hierher drahten.
> Nachrchef 4 B 49909.

**Meaning:** The proposed first part tells the Engineer Inspectorate in
Munich that the two named men left at 7 p.m. as couriers carrying radio
operating documents for `GRUKONACH?02`. The continuation instructs the
recipient to notify that unit and telegraph the arrival back to the sender.

The names `GERAUS` and `MAHRER` remain unidentified; their U and H are not supported across every fit of both alignment models. The reading retains the unexpanded `FELDGR` and singular `ALS KURIER`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-what-is-directly-supported"></a>

### Direct evidence from the second-part copies

All three second-part records contain exactly 136 coordinates. Under the
known partial square, each fixes 67 of 68 plaintext positions. The p158 C2
text is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GRUKONACH?02BENACHRICHTIGENEINTREFFENHIERHERDRAHTENXNACHRCHEF4B49909
```

</details>

The p151 D2 repeat has `GRU1ONACH` at the beginning, and p153 D2 has
`BENACHWICHTIGEN`; the source edition preserves both. The unaltered p158
witness independently supplies the readable forms of both words.

The question mark denotes the observed pair **VF**, whose unassigned square value is **5 or 6**.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-a-separately-linked-conditional-reading-grukonach602"></a>

#### A separately linked conditional reading: GRUKONACH602

The [9 November operational reports](166.md#edition-cases-military-nov9-operational-reports-historical-identification-most-likely-the-6th-reserve-division) use the same **VF** cell for a reserve-division numeral. A contemporary French telegram identifies the matching formation as the **6th Reserve Division**. Under that historical identification, **VF=6**, and both courier fields read **GRUKONACH602** with no additional source-coordinate changes.

This is one historical inference applied through a shared key cell. The base domain remains 5/6; the first-part reconstruction and its association with the continuation retain the assumptions below. The [context certificate](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json) records the external source, its date limits and the earlier p176b application.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-first-part-damage-and-explicit-reconstruction-cost"></a>

### First-part damage and explicit reconstruction cost

The first parts both advertise 268 coordinates but actually preserve 259
and 264 slots. Both visibly contain the six-letter group `VXDVDD`, which
the transcription retains. One overstruck glyph in p162 A1 is masked as a
source erasure; its displayed reading is kept separately.

Comparing the two sources without the key finds a five-slot relative gap:
all 260 possible gap starts were tested, and seven tied starts, 151–157,
leave only two known-coordinate disagreements. This does not locate the
other four slots missing from the longer witness.

For the **stated 134-position candidate**, exact alignment gives:

| Alignment model | p153 E1 | p162 A1 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Retain every source coordinate | Insert 9 slots; change 6 known coordinates; 32 tied minimum fits | Insert 4 slots; change 8 known coordinates; 2 tied minimum fits |
| Delete one received coordinate | Delete 1, insert 10; change 4 known coordinates; 192 tied minimum fits | Delete 1, insert 5; change 6 known coordinates; 14 tied minimum fits |

Every deletion position and tied optimum is retained. A fill of the overstruck p162 glyph is charged separately from observed-coordinate changes.

Within the first model, **123/134 proposed positions** have an unchanged coordinate pair in at least one witness for every combination of minimum fits. Requiring that support under both models gives **118/134**. These counts are conditional on the proposed wording and alignment families. The [certificate](../../experiments/courier_recovery/certificate.json) includes all raw masked-frame readings and exact costs.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-courier-munich-association-source-and-credit"></a>

### Association, source and credit

The two first-part records explicitly say first part of two, and all three
continuations say second part. The p153 D/E headers both read `RVV v N4` on
the same morning; the first-part `2120 (SY)` field also fits the p151 D
`SY v N4` continuation. Both bodies use the same unresolved `GRUKONACH?02`
field, and the instruction to report arrival follows naturally from the
departure notice. These facts support the association, but the typed log
does not explicitly cross-reference the parts as one original transmission.
The direct continuation remains readable independently of that association.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, printed pp151, 153, 158 and 162 / PDF page 154, 156, 161 and 165,
in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
The [source inputs](../../experiments/courier_recovery/inputs.json) give
literal rows, headers and reproducible image rectangles. The Nov7–9 key
retains its historical and George Lasry / coauthor attribution in
[the key register](../../data/keys.json).

Source inspection, repeated-copy recovery, reconstruction and edition: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

```sh
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/build.py --verify
python3 experiments/courier_recovery/verify.py
```

## p162 B1 — General Staff Berlin map-sheet request; coupled quantity and map-scale digits unresolved

**Edition context:** Berlin General Staff map-sheet request.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-map-sheet-request-berlin-general-staff-map-sheet-request"></a>



Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.
The published Nov7–9 period key retains its original attribution.

<a id="source-p162-b1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-map-sheet-request-p162-b1"></a>

### p162 B1

Childs printed p162 (PDF page 165) has header `UKS v ZON`, reception
`03.40 a.m., November 9th`, and `1109 2 TLE`. The printed part label is
`1 TL`; its length field is literally `RICHI-182?`. That final question
mark belongs to the header, not to the encrypted body.

The [source image](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_B_detail.png)
contains **181 visible slots**. Its initial group is the four-character
`DGDD`. The primary **182-slot conditional frame** inserts one unknown
coordinate at source boundary 1, giving `D?GDD`; no observed glyph is
removed. The source identifies a short group but does not determine an
exact internal missing position. The other part of this physical
transmission is not identified here.

The [faded-glyph crop](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_B_faint.png)
needs a separate source qualification: source 110 is provisionally read F
in `VFGGD`, but an E-like reading remains possible. The primary arithmetic
uses the stated F and explicitly pays for changing it. The E/masked
sensitivity below retains the alternative; plaintext fluency is not used
to make the source glyph certain.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 182-slot frame, with the explicitly provisional F transcription:**

```text
STELLVERTRXG?NERJLSTABBERLINXZUSENDUNG?ONJE?0BL??TTERNKAR2E1ZU7?000XB1B2B3C1C2C3D1D2D3E2E3X
```

**Edited output — same frame; two observed substitutions, three printed-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill:**

```text
STELLVERTRXGENERALSTABBERLINXZUSENDUNGVONJE?0BLAETTERNKARTE1ZU7?000XB1B2B3C1C2C3D1D2D3E2E3X
```

</details>

The substitutions are **source 110 F→D** (`J`→`A` in `GENERAL`) and
**source 150 D→V** (`2`→`T` in `KARTE`). The first cost depends on the
provisional F source reading; it is not hidden as an ordinary erasure fill.
Printed source 84 `Z` is filled with A, source 85 dash with V, and source 149
dash with D. The extra model coordinate is filled with D. These are three
different operation classes, and all source offsets are zero-based.

Under that frame and transcription the raw reading fixes **85 / 91
positions**, and the edited layer fixes **89 / 91**.

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited layer, with spacing, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering:**

> Stellvertr. Generalstab Berlin. Zusendung von je ?0 Blättern Karte 1 zu 7?000. B1 B2 B3 C1 C2 C3 D1 D2 D3 E2 E3.

The letter-number sheet list remains literal, and `STELLVERTR` remains
abbreviated. No requested quantity or map scale is silently completed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-map-sheet-request-conditional-digit-reading"></a>

### Conditional digit reading

Under the [shared Nov7–9 digit interpretation](../../experiments/nov7_9_joint_digits/README.md), this requests **50 copies of each listed sheet at 1:75,000**. The alternative square gives 60 copies at 1:76,000. The reference comparison selects the first reading conditionally, with no additional source edit or fill.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-map-sheet-request-conditional-interpretation-linked-numbers-and-source-sensitivity"></a>

### Conditional interpretation: linked numbers and source sensitivity

Both unresolved numerical positions, plaintext 43 and 63, use the **same
missing square cell XA**. The two unused key labels are 5 and 6, so the
complete coupled alternatives are:

| XA label | Other missing cell VF | Quantity field | Scale field |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 5 | 6 | 50 | 1:75000 |
| 6 | 5 | 60 | 1:76000 |

Both assignments decrypt and re-encrypt the complete edited witness.
Mixed quantity/scale pairings are unsupported by this key. No external map
history is used to select one of the two alternatives.

The independent fixed-target audit checks **all 182 insertion boundaries**
under the primary F transcription, retaining the two XA identities rather
than treating the numerical question marks as free independent characters.
Boundaries 0 and 1 tie at two observed substitutions and yield the same
completed ciphertext but different source-origin maps. The first five
boundary costs are **2,2,3,4,4**. Boundary 1 is the displayed convention,
not a unique historical loss location.

A second complete 182-boundary audit treats the doubtful source 110 glyph
as noncoordinate E, hence as a source mask. It has the same two optimum
origins and the same completed reading, with **one observed substitution,
four source-mask fills and one missing-coordinate fill**. The primary
summary retains the more explicit F-based substitution cost; it does not
silently switch to this cheaper interpretation.

The unaltered 181-slot diagnostic, its unpaired coordinate, all five
source-local group placements and both complete global key witnesses are
preserved in the [inputs](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/inputs.json)
and [certificates](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/certificates.json).
The [reproduction guide](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/README.md)
also records prior OCR and key credit. The bounded comparison prices a
supplied template; it is not a claim of blind or historical uniqueness.

## p162 C1 — Wire communications and return instructions

**Edition context:** Wire communications, return instructions and the Tiraspol continuation.

**Related source pages:** [p166 C1](166.md#source-p166-c1), [p166 C2](166.md#source-p166-c2).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-wire-return-source-family-wire-communications-return-instructions-and-the-tiraspol-continuation"></a>



**Source collation and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

The two surviving copies supply complementary evidence. The short first
part on printed p162 overlaps the end of the longer first part on p166,
and their second parts differ at only two source positions. This edition
adds three physical records: **p162 C1, p166 C1 and p166 C2**. The earlier
[p162 C2 edition](#edition-cases-military-tiraspol-border-report) remains a supporting
witness, with its original displays unchanged.

The primary unfilled frames fix **205 of 362 plaintext positions** across
the three records. Copying the independently observed p166 prefix to the
p162 model supplies 156 further labels; supplying one missing p166 `X`
from p162 supplies one more. Those **157 source-linked completions are
counted separately**, because p162 by itself fixes no complete plaintext
pair in the restored 312-coordinate frame. Six distinct observed-source
substitutions produce the optional complete edition: three supported by
the other copies and three lexical choices in the shared p166 prefix.

The [Childs source](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view)
prints p162 C at `09.45 a.m., November 9th`, with an unread recipient
identifier and `v NKJ`, followed by `missed first part of this message`.
The p166 C header reads `UKS v NKJ`, `9.47 a.m., November 9th`,
`0920 (9) 2 TLE`. These receipt times remain distinct. Both full pages and
the enlarged C crops were directly inspected. The exact PDF, pages,
rectangles, dimensions and RGB digests are preserved in
[the source inputs](../../experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/inputs.json);
no unpublished image asset is needed to reproduce the evidence.

<a id="source-p162-c1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-wire-return-source-family-p162-c1"></a>

### p162 C1

The printed body contains **117 coordinates**, and its first-part header
gives no recoverable total length. In the source-linked 312-coordinate
frame, all **195 absent prefix coordinates remain unknown in the primary
layer**. There are 117 half-pairs with one observed p162 coordinate and 39
pairs with neither coordinate present. No complete pair is fixed by this
fragment alone. Its literal odd-length 117-coordinate inverse, including
the unpaired final coordinate, is retained as a diagnostic in the
certificate; it is not used as a readable message or included in the
fixed-position total.

????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????????
```

</details>

Every complete pair retains both source origins. Of the resulting 156

<details>

AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODELSAMITDORTBGERHGRXMOGGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWIESENSEINXSTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

**Edited output — three lexical substitutions at borrowed p166 prefix origins; zero substitutions to the observed p162 fragment:**

```text
AKONACH18XMITTEILTOBDRAHTVERKEHRODESSAXODESSAMITDORTIGERHGRXMOEGLICHXSTOERUNGSPOSTENACKERMANNSOLLVONBRAILAZURRUECKKEHRANGEWIESENSEINXSTOERUNGSPOSTENTIRASPOL
```

**Readable German — complete conditional source-linked edition, preserving the literal wording, separators and labels:**

> Akonach 18 X mitteilt ob Drahtverkehr Odessa X Odessa mit dortiger Hgr X moeglich X Stoerungsposten Ackermann soll von Braila zur Rueckkehr angewiesen sein X Stoerungsposten Tiraspol.

**Conditional interpretation:** The collated text concerns whether wire
communication involving Odessa and the local `Hgr` is possible. It says
that the post labeled Ackermann should have been instructed to return
from Braila, and then names a Tiraspol post. The awkward `MITTEILT`, repeated
`ODESSA`, and `AKONACH18` are retained. This reading does not determine a
person's identity, a precise organizational expansion of `Hgr`, or the
technical duties of a `Stoerungsposten`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-wire-return-source-family-source-only-alignment-and-exact-costs"></a>

### Source-only alignment and exact costs

All indices are zero-based. The geometry is selected from source
coordinates, before introducing a German word target. In each unfilled
p166 gap alias, all **196 contiguous 117-position windows** are compared
with the p162 fragment. Offset **195** is uniquely best at two observed
coordinate disagreements. At that suffix, all **117 possible locations**
for a single absent coordinate are compared: only local gaps **30 and 31**
attain the same two-disagreement minimum.

The overlap contains **114 independently agreeing observed coordinates,
two disagreements and one absent p166 coordinate**. Once the absent
coordinate is copied from p162, the filled strings agree at 115 positions;
one of those matches is supplied from the other copy and is not a 115th
independent agreement. These exact comparisons establish the best match
within the declared single-loss model, without excluding every possible
alternative error history.

| Origin of operation | Original source position | Operation | Plaintext effect | Evidential role |
| --- | ---: | --- | --- | --- |
| p166 C1 | Gap before 225 or 226 | Insert `X` from p162 C1 source 30 or 31 | Completes one raw `O` | Independent source-linked fill; aliases preserved |
| p166 C1 | 246 | `D` → `G` | `ANGEWGESEN` → `ANGEWIESEN` | Supported by p162 C1 source 52; other half of the pair still comes from p166 |
| p166 C1 | 247 | `F` → `D` | `OTOERUNGSPOSTEN` → `STOERUNGSPOSTEN` | Supported by p162 C1 source 53; other half of the pair still comes from p166 |
| p166 C1 | 160 | `D` → `X` | `ODELSA` → `ODESSA` | Optional lexical correction; the earlier `ODESSA` is already raw |
| p166 C1 | 161 | `X` → `G` | `DORTBGER` → `DORTIGER` | Optional lexical correction in borrowed prefix |
| p166 C1 | 162 | `G` → `V` | `MOGGLICH` → `MOEGLICH` | Optional lexical correction in borrowed prefix |
| p166 C2 | 84 | `F` → `V` | `ROZM` → `ROEM` | Supported by the complete raw p162 C2 pair |

The three prefix corrections appear in both readable first parts, but
there are only **three distinct corrected received coordinates**, all
from p166. Counting them a second time as p162 edits would confuse a
copied reading with independent evidence. The entire 117-coordinate p162
fragment remains unchanged throughout.

| New physical record | Printed coordinates | Modeled coordinates | Primary fixed labels | Source-linked labels added | Optional fixed labels |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| p162 C1 | 117 | 312 | 0 / 156 | 156 | 156 / 156 |
| p166 C1 | 311 | 312 | 155 / 156 | 1 | 156 / 156 |
| p166 C2 | 100 | 100 | 50 / 50 | 0 | 50 / 50 |
| Total | 528 | 724 | **205 / 362** | **157** | **362 / 362** |

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov9-wire-return-source-family-reproduction-and-credit"></a>

### Reproduction and credit

The [certificate](../../experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/certificates.json)
contains the primary unfilled records, both gap aliases, every complete
pair's two coordinate origins, all source-only costs, the six unique
observed substitutions, the independent gap witness, native odd-frame
diagnostics and preserved OCR comparisons. Earlier OCR counted 307
coordinates for p166 C1; the actual printed source has 311. Restoring
misread digital transcription is kept separate from the one still absent
manuscript coordinate. Neither the published key nor the core challenge
messages are changed.

```sh
python experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/verify.py --verify
python experiments/nov9_wire_return_source_family/verify.py --verify --pdf /tmp/adfgvx-childs.pdf
```

Without the PDF argument, the verifier explicitly reports that source
pixel reproduction is skipped; all source, alignment, origin, cipher,
round-trip and display assertions still run. With the PDF argument, both
reviewed crop RGB digests are reproduced from the pinned source.

The manuscript source is **J. Rives Childs**. Published period-key credit
remains with **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker** (2016)
and George Lasry's 2017 disclosure, as recorded in the unchanged key
metadata. This is source restoration and explicit editorial collation by
**icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**, with prior OCR and the earlier p162 C2
edition preserved.

<a id="edition-cases-military-tiraspol-border-report"></a>

## p162 C2 — Tiraspol reports machine-gun fire at the border; first part unavailable

**Edition context:** Tiraspol fragment: fire at the border.

<a id="edition-cases-military-tiraspol-border-report-tiraspol-fragment-fire-at-the-border"></a>



Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

<a id="source-p162-c2"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-tiraspol-border-report-p162-c2"></a>

### p162 C2

Childs printed p162 (PDF page 165), C, has an unknown recipient identifier,
`v NKJ`, and receipt `09.45 a.m., November 9th`. The page explicitly says
`missed first part of this message`. A separate 117-coordinate C1 fragment
remains unread and is excluded from the three new accepted records in
this package. The following body is independently labeled `2 TL RICHI-100`.

The [source crop](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_C_detail.png)
contains **100 slots**, including a printed dash at source 36 in `D-XDF`.
The unchanged published **Nov7–9** key gives 49 of 50 fixed positions.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 100-slot frame:**

```text
TIRASPOLERHIEL?MXGXFEUERANDERGRENZEXAKONACH17ROEM4
```

**Edited output — one printed-dash fill, with no observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
TIRASPOLERHIELTMXGXFEUERANDERGRENZEXAKONACH17ROEM4
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited layer, with spacing, punctuation and conventional umlaut rendering:**

> Tiraspol erhielt M. G. Feuer an der Grenze. Akonach 17 Röm. 4.

The single fill supplies the T in `ERHIELT`; the edited body has **50 / 50
fixed positions** and re-encrypts exactly under the recorded source repair.
The terminal cleartext `NKJ UM` is outside the cipher frame and these counts.

<a id="edition-cases-military-tiraspol-border-report-scope-and-uncertainty"></a>

### Scope and uncertainty

The fragment reports `M G FEUER` at a border, with the literal label
`TIRASPOL`. It does not identify a specific person, unit, border or event
from outside history. The incomplete surrounding message is not silently
restored from this short clause. The ending `AKONACH17ROEM4` remains
unexpanded, and all numeral labels remain literal.

The earlier unreviewed OCR screen already identified this body; this edition
adds source inspection and explicit fill accounting. Published key credit
and prior candidate status are retained in the
[inputs](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/certificates.json)
and [reproduction guide](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/README.md).
No first historical decipherment priority is claimed.

A later [p162/p166 source-family collation](#edition-cases-radio-nov9-wire-return-source-family) conditionally restores the p162 C1 prefix from the independently observed p166 copy and supplies a received-coordinate witness for this C2 dash fill. The original raw, edited and readable displays above remain unchanged.

## p162 D1 — German embassy Constantinople; signature Stumm, part1 only

**Edition context:** Constantinople embassy address and Stumm signature.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-embassy-signature-constantinople-embassy-address-and-stumm-signature"></a>



Source edition and verification: **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

<a id="source-p162-d1"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-embassy-signature-p162-d1"></a>

### p162 D1

Childs printed p162 (PDF page 165), D, has header `XYZ v LP`, receipt
`06.12 a.m., November 10th`, and the literal origin field
`1330 (8/13) 2 TEILE`. The unusual `8/13` is retained as printed, without
turning it into an assumed calendar date. The surviving body is labeled
`1 TL RICHI-100`; the other part is not identified here.

The [source crop](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/sources/p162_D_detail.png)
contains **100 slots**, including printed C glyphs at source 22, 37 and 79.
Those noncoordinate letters are kept in the literal transcript and each
represented by one mask in the analysis. The source does not acquire a
different length. It decodes under the unchanged published **Nov7–9** key,
although its receipt header is 10 November.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native 100-slot frame with the three printed C glyphs masked:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTA??INOPELXUNTERSCHRIF?STUMMX
```

**Edited output — three printed-invalid-glyph fills, with no observed-coordinate substitutions:**

```text
DEUTSCHEBOTSCHAFTKONSTANTINOPELXUNTERSCHRIFTSTUMMX
```

</details>

**Readable German — exact nonseparator labels of the edited layer, with spacing and punctuation:**

> Deutsche Botschaft Konstantinopel. Unterschrift Stumm.

The fills restore N and T in `KONSTANTINOPEL` and T in `UNTERSCHRIFT`.
The native raw layer fixes **47 / 50 positions**; the edited layer fixes
**50 / 50** and re-encrypts exactly with those three source masks filled.

<a id="edition-cases-people-constantinople-embassy-signature-scope-and-credit"></a>

### Scope and credit

This is an address/signature fragment. It does not establish the missing
substantive request, a particular person's identity or the association of
another nearby telegram merely because the name STUMM appears there.
The original part label and odd origin field remain visible.

The earlier OCR-derived candidate already identified the embassy/signature
wording. This source edition retains that earlier work and the published
key's attribution; it makes no first historical decipherment claim. The
[inputs](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/inputs.json),
[certificates](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/certificates.json)
and [reproduction guide](../../experiments/nov8_map_and_boundary/README.md)
retain the raw glyphs, every source offset and complete re-encryption witnesses.
